case_title: Barku Bhavrao Bhaskar v. State of Maharashtra
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.34; Arms Act s.27
aggravating_circumstances: Motive for murder, blood stains on shirt, recovery of body at instance of accused
neutral_facts: The accused was the last person seen with the victim, a female child aged about 6 years. The victim was last seen with the accused at her residence. A child witness reported seeing the accused and the victim together. The accused led the authorities to the victim's body, which was found covered with stones and branches. The victim sustained severe head and ear injuries, and the post-mortem report indicated the injuries were antemortem. Bloodstains on the accused's shirt matched the victim's blood group. The accused had a motive for murder due to a dispute over wages. The accused made an extra-judicial confession admitting to the crime. The accused's shirt was recovered at his instance, and no injuries were found on his body, ruling out self-inflicted bloodstains. The accused was found to have led the authorities to the victim's body, which was covered with stones and branches.
